summary.headline: The Zoning Board granted side setback relief for 34 Turnpike Road conditioned on Board of Health septic approval.
summary.summary: The Southborough Zoning Board of Appeals met to address multiple property applications and zoning revisions. The board approved an applicant request to withdraw an application for 22 Newton Street without prejudice. Members also debated draft updates to the town two-family zoning bylaw to remove a two-year residency waiting period and refine dimensional requirements. Finally, the board approved a 1.3-foot side setback relief for 34 Turnpike Road after addressing septic proximity concerns and abutter objections regarding bedroom count and Title 5 compliance.

topics.title: 22 Newton Street withdrawal request
topics.summary: The applicant for 22 Newton Street requested to withdraw their application without prejudice. The proposal previously involved constructing a two-car garage that blocked access to the backyard. The board voted to grant the withdrawal without prejudice so the homeowner can reconsider options.
key_details: Prior proposal involved constructing a two-car garage

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The board reviewed and approved the draft meeting minutes from its previous meeting on May 6.
key_details: Approved minutes of the May 6 meeting with minor amendments

topics.title: Two-family zoning bylaw update discussion
topics.summary: Board members reviewed draft revisions to the two-family zoning bylaw stemming from recent updates to accessory dwelling unit bylaws. Discussion focused on eliminating the requirement that a homeowner must reside in a newly constructed home for two years before converting it into a two-family dwelling. Members also discussed curb cut limitations, lot size rules, and harmonizing definitions with the Planning Board ahead of fall Town Meeting.
key_details: Bylaw currently requires a two-year wait before adding a second unit in newly constructed homes
Current regulations require a minimum lot size of 15,000 square feet for two-family dwellings
Board plans to coordinate revised draft language with the Planning Board in July
topics.outcome: Discussion held; staff and board members will refine draft language for the July 15 meeting

topics.title: 34 Turnpike Road setback relief and as-built modification
topics.summary: The board resumed a public hearing on an addition at 34 Turnpike Road where as-built construction deviated from permitted plans. To resolve an unauthorized foundation bump-out encroaching on septic system setbacks, the contractor proposed cutting back the foundation at grade, filling the void with flowable fill, and supporting the upper floor with an interior steel beam. The applicant also requested dimensional relief for the side setback, which measured 13.9 feet instead of the required 15 feet. After hearing abutter objections concerning overall house size and septic capacity, the board approved the 1.3-foot setback relief on the condition that the Board of Health reviews and certifies the septic capacity.
key_details: Foundation bump-out of approximately 5 by 10 feet encroached on septic system setbacks and must be removed at grade
Requested side setback relief for an as-built distance of 13.9 feet versus the required 15 feet (a 1.3-foot encroachment)
Approval is conditioned on explicit Board of Health confirmation that the septic capacity meets the dwelling bedroom count
Town planner noted a written decision will be filed within two weeks, initiating a 20-day appeal period
topics.why_it_matters: The decision resolves a zoning non-conformity on an expanded home while ensuring the septic system is verified by health officials to protect neighborhood ground conditions.

votes.motion: Withdraw the application for 22 Newton Street without prejudice
Close the public hearing for 34 Turnpike Road
Approve the request for 1.3 feet of side setback relief for 34 Turnpike Road subject to review and approval by the Board of Health confirming septic system capacity meets the bedroom count

public_comment.summary: A representative for the abutting property owner at 32 Turnpike Road objected to the expansion of 34 Turnpike Road, stating the lot historically housed a 750-square-foot dwelling with zero road frontage and argued that the current structure amounts to an unpermitted four-bedroom house. He urged the board to postpone granting zoning relief until the Board of Health formally reviews the septic system under Title 5.

upcoming.what: Next Zoning Board of Appeals meeting featuring three new hearings, including two variances and one special permit for Costco lighting and retaining walls
